text:
Commander night at Tom Beloy's, Saturday 22 August, three-player pod: me on Ur-Dragon, Alex on a mono-red Tannuk, Steadfast Second warp deck, Tom on Merfolk.

Alex played Blood Moon on turn two or three and that was the game. Every nonbasic I own became a Mountain. I could not cast Smothering Tithe, could not cast the red-green dragons, could not cast anything multicoloured. I was reduced to the all-red dragons only.

What I actually did with it: Moltensteel Dragon, and at the end I paid sixteen life to pump it and hit Alex for twelve. If I was locked out anyway, he was going to feel it.

Blood Moon is a broken card in my view and I am not building around it. At bracket 3+ some people run that stuff and that is the deal. So I am not calling this a deck problem in the sense of needing an answer to Blood Moon.

The real lesson is the mana base and I want it audited holistically: how many basics I run and whether land tutors can whiff, whether the pip spread across the lands actually matches what the dragons demand rather than just being generic fixing, and whether I am taking tempo hits from enters-tapped lands where an untapped source would do. Tap lands are fine to a degree.

The rest of the deck I am happy with - removal, treasures, discounts, haste, card draw are all solid. The bottleneck is mana consistency, not card selection.

Commander night at Oliver's, Tuesday 25 August, five-player pod: Oliver, Ryan, Tom, Alex and me. I was in seat 4. WIN — but see below, because the deck did not earn it.

FIRST GAME ON THE NEW LAND BASE. I raised the mana base 31 -> 36 the same day, five lands in and dragons out. My reaction to the old count was disbelief that it ever ran at 31.

It did not help. Mulliganed once (I did not record why). Kept about three lands, a dragon cost-reducer (I did not note which one) and The Ur-Dragon, with Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm and more six-drops behind it. Then the mana never arrived — I was sitting on 4-5 lands on turns 6 and 7, three to five lands behind the curve. For comparison the table was on 8-10 lands plus dorks, and Alex was tapping for something like 12 mana on turns 4-5 while I had 4.

The cost-reducer got removed, so the discount engine never did its job. After that it was repeated creature wipes — board established, board erased, repeat. A board did start to come together late and I got in some damage and some political leverage.

HOW I WON: not as a threat. I stayed off the radar, let the other four grind each other down, and closed at the end. Not my proudest moment — you don't want to win like that. And it is the shape of most of my recent wins.

My own read: the deck did not win, the table's attrition won and I was the last one standing. That works in a five-pod and will not repeat against a tighter table.

The mana deficit is not one bad night — I have been three to five lands behind curve consistently across the last four or five games. What it does downstream is that cards sit in my hand that are castable eventually, so the play gets telegraphed a turn or two ahead, and by the time the mana is there the piece has been answered.

The pod runs heavy creature removal and heavy board wipes, and this deck generates no value on the way down.

Game 2 of three at Oliver's, five-player pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan.

FIRST VALIDATION GAME for the statistical-analysis refactoring process. v1.0.0
was 31 lands and thin rocks; v1.0.1 added lands and fixing; v1.0.2 swapped the
mana density toward more dorks and rocks. The mana worked.

Mulliganed into a strong hand. Turn one land into Sol Ring and Arcane Signet —
four mana on turn one. Turn two Bloom Tender, five available in a five-colour
deck.

Curve after that: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm (copies dragons), Gadrak, the
Crown-Scourge (Treasure on creature death), Terror of the Peaks (three damage
each to three targets on the swing). Two copies of Terror is twenty targeted
damage.

Played Gadrak a turn too early and telegraphed the whole thing. Once the table
read "Sean is swinging for 28 in the air," they converged immediately: Tom
removed all three artifacts so Gadrak could not activate (needs four), Alex
fought the dragons with his fight deck, Ryan removed more, Tom pinged with
Purphoros.

Loss.

Three piloting lessons:
1. SPEED TRAP — I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could
   actually present lethal.
2. POLITICS MISS — if I am getting that big that fast I need alliances, or I am
   the solo target by definition.
3. I CUT PROTECTION AND COUNTERS FOR SPEED, and it showed. Targeted removal and
   board wipes take the deck apart now.

Research I want done on this deck:
(a) Dragons that grant haste to the board — the problem is speed, not size.
(b) Haste enablers generally. Terror has to swing the turn it lands, not sit.
(c) Protection density — some lock-down (equipment indestructible?) that does
    not cost me dragon slots.
(d) A TABLE POLITICS LAYER for the pilot's manual. When you are the Targaryen
    with the dragon army, think like Daenerys about threat management: read the
    room, form alliances, hold back a swing to signal you are not the only
    problem at the table.

All four feed one issue: speed without protection or politics makes me the
obvious kill target before I can close.
